title: File system requirements
idea: Scoping an in-memory file system means fixing which operations users get on a tree of directories and files, how paths are written, and what v1 leaves out.
points: Users make directories, create files, list, move, rename and delete them.
Every operation takes an absolute path such as `/home/ada/cv.pdf`.
Directory size and name search walk the whole subtree below a path.
Assume one process, data in memory, and many readers with fewer writers.

hero.title: Actors and use cases in v1

edges.caption: A user changes the tree: makes folders, adds files, moves, renames and deletes.
A user also reads it: lists a folder, asks a folder's total size, or finds files by name.

edges.label: uses
edges.caption: Every operation starts by turning a path string into a node, or failing with a clear error.

edges.label: uses
edges.caption: Reads resolve paths the same way, so one parser serves every use case.
The tree has exactly one root. Each node has one parent, so it can never loop.
Permissions, symbolic links and saving to disk are cut from v1. Say this to the interviewer.

code.title: Scope and path rules
code.caption: The v1 scope as an enum, and the path rules as a check you can run against sample paths.

walk.text: Print every use case with its scope tag and the actor who needs it.
Run six sample paths through the path rules, including bad ones.
Seven use cases are in v1. Each one becomes a method later.
Three are named and cut, so the boundary is written down.
Paths must be absolute, and no name between slashes may be empty.
A dot stays put; two dots climb one level but never above the root.

pitfalls: Agree whether paths are absolute only, or relative to a current directory.
Ask if delete on a non-empty directory is recursive or refused.
Name what is out of scope, such as permissions and links, before designing.

quiz.q: The interviewer adds symbolic links late. Which v1 promise do they break?
options: Every path must start with a slash
One parent per node, so every walk ends
Directory names are sorted when listed
Files have a size in bytes
quiz.why: A link can point at its own ancestor. Then a recursive size or search could loop forever unless it tracks visited nodes.

takeaway: Fix the operations, the path rules and the cut list before any class.
